Finnish environmental and support services group, headquartered in Helsinki, running waste management and recycling, industrial cleaning, facility services (property maintenance, cleaning, security-adjacent support) and environmental products for customers in Finland, Sweden and the Baltics. Customers are mostly businesses, municipalities and public bodies, paid on recurring service contracts, with annual revenue of roughly EUR 800 million and about 7,000 to 8,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (LAT1V), founded in 1905. B2B brand, well known in Finland but little consumer awareness elsewhere.

Chinese smartphone, tablet, wearable and AIoT design house based in Shanghai. As an original design manufacturer it designs devices that other brands then sell under their own names, and it has worked for large handset makers such as Xiaomi, Samsung, OPPO and Lenovo, earning revenue from design and manufacturing fees. Founded in 2005, with research centres and factories in China and India. Shares trade on a mainland Chinese exchange. B2B supplier, so the brand is almost unknown to consumers, though its products are widely sold under other labels.

Mortgage real estate investment trust based in New York and listed on the NYSE (MFA). It invests in residential mortgage assets, mainly non-agency and non-qualified mortgage loans, plus securities and loans for single-family rental, and it earns money from net interest spread and fees. It owns a lending arm, Lima One Capital, which makes short-term investor loans for property flips and rentals, and manages a portfolio worth many billions of dollars. Founded in 1998. Financial-markets brand with essentially no consumer visibility, and it has few obvious reasons to sponsor motorsport.

Commercial bank headquartered in Blantyre, one of the two or three largest banks in Malawi, offering retail and corporate banking, savings and current accounts, loans, trade finance, cards and mobile banking through a national branch network. Customers are individuals, small businesses, corporates and government bodies, paid through interest margins and fees. Founded in 1971, listed on the Malawi Stock Exchange, with Press Corporation as the controlling shareholder. Well-known domestic brand with strong local awareness, but its reach is limited to Malawi and a small economy.

Connecticut-based real estate finance company, listed on NYSE American (SACH), that makes short-term secured loans to real estate investors who renovate or build residential and commercial property in the US Northeast and Mid-Atlantic. Loans are typically asset-backed hard-money loans of 12 months or so, and income comes from interest, origination fees and some rental and property sales. Structured as a REIT with a small team and a loan book of a few hundred million dollars. Niche lender, essentially no consumer brand awareness and small marketing budgets.

Slovenia's largest insurer, Zavarovalnica Triglav, based in Ljubljana. It sells motor, property, accident, health and life insurance and pension products to individuals and businesses, and has subsidiaries in Croatia, Serbia, Bosnia, North Macedonia, Montenegro and Kosovo, making it a leading player across the Adriatic region with roughly EUR 1.5 billion of annual premiums. Listed on the Ljubljana Stock Exchange. Founded in 1900. Strong household-name brand in Slovenia and the former Yugoslav markets, and a long-standing sponsor of Slovenian sport.

Offshore drilling contractor that owns and operates ultra-deepwater drillships and premium jackup rigs, leasing them with crews to oil and gas majors and national oil companies for exploration and development wells. Founded in 2008 and registered in Bermuda, with operating offices in Houston, Singapore and elsewhere; it emerged from bankruptcy in 2016 and trades over the counter. Revenue depends on day rates and contract backlog, and the fleet is small compared with Transocean or Valaris. B2B business with no consumer profile.

Indian education company based in Chennai, listed on the NSE and BSE, offering online and classroom coaching for competitive exams and professional courses. Its Veranda Race and Veranda IAS brands prepare students for banking, civil service and other government jobs, and it also teaches accounting and finance qualifications such as CA, CMA and ACCA through acquired institutes, plus skilling and school products. Customers are students and graduates paying course fees, mostly in South India. Recognisable among exam aspirants but modest overall consumer brand scale.

Maker of laptops and desktop systems with augmented and virtual reality displays, sold to schools, colleges and career-training programmes in the US and abroad. Its zSpace platform uses tracked glasses and a stylus so students can manipulate 3D models, with software for science, medical and technical education. Based in San Jose, founded in 2007, and listed on Nasdaq (ZSPC) since its 2025 IPO. Customers are education institutions and training providers buying hardware, software subscriptions and content. Specialised B2B edtech brand with little public recognition.

Swiss real estate company based in Zug, listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange, owning and developing commercial and mixed-use property in canton Zug. Its holdings include the Metalli shopping and service centre in Zug town and the Suurstoffi district in Risch Rotkreuz, plus hotel operations such as the Parkhotel Zug. Income comes from rents and hotel operations. Majority controlled by the Zug-based Zuger family circle. Mid-sized property company with a regional rather than national profile and little consumer brand awareness.

Indian arm of the AkzoNobel paints group, best known for the Dulux brand, with decorative paints for homes plus industrial coatings, powder coatings and protective coatings. Sells through a large dealer network and tinting machines across India, and is a top-three player in decorative paint. Revenue around INR 40 billion, listed on the NSE and BSE, with AkzoNobel as majority owner; it announced a plan for JSW Paints to take over the Dulux business in India in 2025. Strong consumer brand in India.

Real estate investment trust in Dubai, listed on the Dubai Financial Market, managed by Al Mal Capital, an investment bank and asset manager. It holds income-producing property in the UAE and rents it to commercial tenants, paying investors dividends from rental income. A small, regional vehicle with only a handful of assets. Mostly institutional and retail investors in the Gulf know it; it has no consumer brand and little public marketing.

Australian leisure group listed on the ASX (ALG) that owns and operates Main Event, a chain of roughly 50 to 60 family entertainment centres in the United States (bowling, arcade games, laser tag, food and drink), after selling off its theme parks and health clubs. Customers are US families and corporate event groups. The company has been headquartered in Sydney but is closely tied to Texas-based Main Event. Strong regional consumer brand in the US, especially in Texas, and sponsorship is likely to be considered in the US.

Web accessibility company based in Tucson, listed on Nasdaq (AEYE), selling a software-as-a-service platform that scans websites, fixes issues automatically and checks compliance with accessibility rules such as WCAG and the ADA. It works with thousands of customers, including retailers, publishers and public bodies, on subscription pricing, and reports annual revenue of roughly USD 30 to 40 million. Founded in 2005 and led by Todd Bankofier. B2B software with little consumer awareness, though many sites run its tools.

Shenzhen-based consumer electronics brand known for smartphone chargers, power banks, cables, car accessories, robot vacuums and small gadgets, sold mostly through Amazon and other online marketplaces around the world, especially in North America, Europe and Japan. Amazon removed many of its listings in 2021 during a crackdown on fake reviews, which hurt sales.

Financial niche vehicle with no consumer profile and no obvious need for brand sponsorship.

Vietnamese joint-stock commercial bank, branded LPBank since 2024 and formerly LienVietPostBank, with its network built on the Vietnam Post offices and listed on Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (LPB). It offers retail and SME banking, deposits, loans, cards, digital banking and remittances through hundreds of branches and post-office counters, with total assets above VND 400 trillion. Customers are individuals and small firms across Vietnam. Recognisable domestic retail bank brand, with moderate to high national awareness.

UK-listed business services group (AIM: MRL) providing compliance, testing and inspection services: fire safety, health and safety, water hygiene, air quality and building safety, plus employee screening and software. Customers are UK businesses, housing associations, hospitals, schools and public bodies, mostly on recurring contracts. Revenue is around GBP 500 million, built through many acquisitions since the 2010s, and headquartered in London. B2B brand with low consumer awareness and no history of major sports sponsorship.

Maker of industrial wireless broadband radios used in oil and gas, mining, utilities, defence and smart-city networks, sold as point-to-point and point-to-multipoint systems through integrators and distributors in North America, the Middle East and Africa. Originally founded in Markham, Ontario, and listed on the Toronto exchange (RDL); the record shows an Austin, Texas address. Revenue is small, in the tens of millions of dollars. B2B equipment supplier with little public profile and limited marketing budget.

Chinese consumer finance technology company based in Shanghai that uses data analytics to match borrowers with lending partners. Its Vcredit app offers small cash loans and instalment credit to individuals, and it also provides credit risk services to banks and microlenders. Revenue comes from loan facilitation and technology service fees. It operates mainly in China, where tighter regulation of online lending has constrained the business. Recognised in Chinese consumer credit but regulation limits consumer brand marketing, and it has no presence outside China.

Euronext Brussels-listed real estate investment company (a Belgian regulated REIT) that owns high-street retail property in Belgium, mainly shops in the prime shopping streets of Antwerp, Brussels, Bruges, Ghent and other cities, let to fashion and consumer brands on long leases. Based in Antwerp and part of the Vastned retail property group, which has Dutch roots. Rental income funds the dividend, and the portfolio is worth a few hundred million euros. Property company with no consumer brand awareness.

UK cleantech company, listed on AIM, developing polymer technology for textiles and filtration. Its Xorb microfibre filters capture microplastics shed by washing machines and its earlier XOrb polymer bead washing system reduced water, energy and detergent use in commercial laundries. Customers are appliance and laundry makers, with revenue from licensing and product sales still small. Based in Rotherham, South Yorkshire, spun out from the University of Leeds in 2007. Niche B2B brand known in sustainability circles.

Chinese financial technology and software company in Shenzhen, listed on the Shenzhen ChiNext board, that builds core banking, risk, credit, data and digital transformation systems for banks, insurers and other financial institutions, mostly in China. Its customers include large state-owned banks and joint-stock banks, and revenue comes from project software, maintenance and service fees. Founded in 1993 and part of the larger Shenzhen software industry. B2B supplier with little recognition among consumers.

Net lease real estate investment trust listed on the NYSE (PINE) that owns single-tenant retail properties let to national tenants such as Lowe's, Dick's Sporting Goods, Walmart and Wawa, mostly on long leases with annual rent escalators. Portfolio of about 150 properties across the US with a market value of roughly USD 300 million. Pure investment vehicle with no consumer brand.

Chinese consumer electronics group, headquartered in Changsha, Hunan, best known for Anker charging products, plus Soundcore audio, eufy smart home and robot vacuums, Nebula projectors and Ankermake 3D printers, sold through Amazon, retailers and its own sites in over 100 countries. Founded in 2011 by former Google engineer Steven Yang, listed on the Shenzhen ChiNext board, with revenue of about CNY 20 billion or more. Strong global consumer brand, especially in online retail, and already sponsors sport and esports.

District heating company in Kaunas, Lithuania's second-largest city, that produces heat and some electricity (including from biomass and a waste-to-energy plant) and delivers it to homes and businesses through a pipe network, with revenue from regulated heating tariffs. Calabasas, California-based commercial real estate brokerage (NYSE: MMI), one of the largest US firms focused on private-client investment sales, with several thousand agents and roughly 80 offices in the US and Canada. It earns commissions on sales of apartment buildings, retail, office and industrial properties, plus financing placement and advisory fees. Founded in 1971. Mainly known to property investors and owners rather than consumers, with moderate brand recognition in US commercial real estate.

Maker of ultrasonic surgical devices, led by the BoneScalpel for precise bone cutting and the SonaStar for tissue removal, used in neurosurgery, spine, plastic surgery and wound care. Based in Farmingdale, New York, it was listed on Nasdaq (MSON) and was acquired by Bioventus in 2021 for roughly USD 500 million after a competing bid from a Chinese investor. Sold to hospitals through surgeons and specialist sales representatives, with annual sales of around USD 70 to 80 million. B2B medical-device brand with no consumer awareness.

Sava Re, Slovenia's largest reinsurer, based in Ljubljana and listed on the Ljubljana Stock Exchange. It provides reinsurance to insurers worldwide and operates a group that includes life and non-life insurance subsidiaries across South-East Europe (Croatia, Serbia, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Bosnia), with premiums of around EUR 600 million. Founded in 1990 as Pozavarovalnica Sava. B2B reinsurance brand known mainly to financial markets, with little consumer visibility.

UK holding company, quoted on AIM, which acquires and holds software businesses serving niche markets, including e-commerce and print-related software, in a permanent-capital 'forever' model rather than a traditional private equity exit model. Based in Manchester, and headed by software entrepreneurs. Customers are small and mid-sized companies buying subscription software. It has been described as a UK compounder-style acquirer. B2B with little consumer profile and few reasons to sponsor motorsport.

British maritime technology company, listed on AIM (SRT), that designs and sells AIS transponders, vessel tracking and maritime domain awareness systems for coastal states, ports and navies, along with shipborne tracking devices. Governments and security agencies are the main customers, including a flagship contract with the Government of Mexico, and it also sells shipborne transponders and an e-navigation software platform. Based in Midsomer Norton near Bath. B2B and government supplier with low public awareness.

Australia's largest diversified property group, listed on the ASX (SGP) and based in Sydney. It develops master-planned residential communities, retirement living villages, retail town centres, logistics and workplace properties across Australia, and holds assets worth well over AUD 15 billion. Revenue comes from land and home sales, rents and fund management. Founded in 1952. Strong consumer brand in Australia through its community estates and shopping centres, and it has done sports sponsorship in Australia.

South Korean children's entertainment company behind the Baby Shark song and animation, the most viewed video in YouTube history, plus Pinkfong's Wonderstar and other children's characters, educational apps, mobile games, toys and licensed products. Based in Seoul and formerly called SmartStudy. Revenue comes from advertising on YouTube, licensing, app subscriptions and merchandise sold in many countries. Very strong global brand recognition among families and preschool audiences, which suits family-oriented partnerships rather than adult-targeted motorsport.

Canadian trucking and logistics company providing truckload, less-than-truckload and brokerage freight services in Canada and across the US border, with a fleet of tractors and trailers and terminals in Ontario and the US. Founded in 2007 and based near Toronto in Bolton, Ontario, although the record shows a California address. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (TTR). Customers are manufacturers and retailers that ship goods, and revenue is around CAD 300 million. B2B transport brand with low public recognition.

Canadian real estate technology and brokerage company, based in Vancouver and listed on the TSX Venture Exchange, offering commercial real estate brokerage and property technology tools for investors, owners and tenants, with revenue from brokerage commissions and service fees. It is a small company that has grown partly through acquisitions of brokerages and property management businesses. Largely unknown outside property-industry users in Canada and no consumer profile, so sponsorship fit is weak. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Romanian software and technology group, based in Cluj-Napoca and listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange (AROBS). It builds custom software, embedded systems and cloud and AI products for customers in automotive, aerospace, banking, retail and telecom, with offices across Romania, Germany, the Netherlands and the US after a string of acquisitions. Revenue is in the order of RON 1 billion. Founded in 1998. Mid-sized B2B technology firm with little consumer awareness outside Romania.

Export Import Bank of Bangladesh, a commercial bank founded in 1999 and headquartered in Dhaka, operating on Islamic Shariah principles. It provides retail, SME and corporate banking, trade finance, remittance and agricultural financing through over 100 branches and ATMs, and it is listed on the Dhaka and Chittagong stock exchanges. Customers are Bangladeshi individuals and businesses, with income from profit-sharing margins and fees. Known as a mid-sized private commercial bank in Bangladesh, with moderate domestic brand awareness.

Chinese live-streaming and social video platform, Inke, run from Beijing and listed in Hong Kong (3700). It launched in 2015 and once ranked among China's leading livestreaming apps, though audiences have fallen with competition from Douyin and Kuaishou. Consumer app brand in China only, with a young audience.

Austin, Texas real estate company listed on Nasdaq (STRS), best known for developing the Lantana and Barton Creek communities in south-west Austin, including the Barton Creek Village retail centre, the W Austin hotel and ACL Live at the Moody Theater, a concert venue it co-owns. Russia's leading online classifieds platform, based in Moscow, where users list and buy cars, property, jobs, services and second-hand goods, with tens of millions of monthly users. Consumer-facing brand in a few US states, with moderate awareness.

Operator of private prisons, detention centres and residential reentry facilities for US federal, state and local governments, plus community corrections services, based in Nashville, Tennessee and listed on the NYSE (CXW). Water treatment company headquartered in Pittsburgh, supplying equipment, filtration, chemicals and services for municipal and industrial water and wastewater customers, with brands including Wallace & Tiernan, Neptune Benson and Memcor. Customers include utilities, factories and pool operators. B2B brand with limited consumer awareness.

UK full-fibre broadband provider based in London, building fibre-to-the-premises networks and selling gigabit broadband to households and businesses, initially in London and later in other parts of southern England, passing hundreds of thousands of homes. Funded by infrastructure and institutional investors rather than a corporate parent. Competes with Openreach, Virgin Media and CityFibre as an altnet. Consumer-facing brand in its coverage areas, though not nationally known and with a small marketing budget.

Chinese online agricultural products marketplace, Meicai, based in Beijing, that supplies fresh vegetables, meat and other produce to restaurants, small grocers and canteens, using a platform that connects farm suppliers with buyers and delivers from its own warehouses. Founded in 2014 by Liu Chuanjun, with backing from Tiger Global, Hillhouse, Tencent and others. It has cut operations in recent years amid losses. B2B brand little known to consumers.

Saudi government development body, based in Riyadh, that oversees and coordinates the kingdom's specialised development funds and banks (including the Saudi Industrial Development Fund, Real Estate Development Fund and Agricultural Development Fund) to support Vision 2030 goals through subsidised lending to industry, mining, housing, tourism and SMEs. Established in 2017 and chaired by the Prime Minister. State-owned, so an institutional brand with low consumer visibility but relevance to national programmes.

Japanese healthcare services and care company based in Tokyo, known as Nichii Gakkan, one of Japan's largest providers of medical office outsourcing (hospital billing and administration), home nursing care, elderly care homes, childcare and education services. Customers are hospitals, local governments and elderly residents, paid by care insurance and fees. It was taken private in a buyout led by Bain Capital. Well-known domestic care brand with a large workforce, but mainly B2B and domestic.

Palo Alto blood-testing startup founded in 2003 by Elizabeth Holmes, which claimed to run hundreds of tests from a few drops of blood using its Edison devices. Backed by Walgreens, Safeway and investors valuing it at USD 9 billion. Defunct and infamous; a clearly toxic brand not available for sponsorship.

Australian lithium processing company, a subsidiary of China's Tianqi Lithium, operating the Kwinana lithium hydroxide plant in Western Australia, with a design capacity of 24,000 tonnes a year, and linked to the Greenbushes lithium mine through Tianqi's shareholding in Talison. B2B commodity producer without consumer awareness.

Canadian cannabis company based in Leamington, Ontario, that grew medical and recreational cannabis and sold brands such as Solei, Good Supply and Broken Coast, and owned CC Pharma, a German pharmaceutical distributor. It merged with Tilray in April 2021 to create one of the world's largest cannabis companies, now called Tilray Brands. Customers include retail consumers, pharmacies and wholesale buyers. The Aphria name now sits inside Tilray, and cannabis exposure limits sports sponsorship.

Canadian gold exploration and development company based in Toronto that held the Bateman Gold Project at the former Bateman mine in the Red Lake district of northwestern Ontario, working to bring a mine into production as a mid-tier operation. Biomat USA is a US network of plasma donation centres run by Grifols, the Spanish pharmaceutical and blood-products company, operating roughly 200 centres across the United States. Donors are paid for plasma, which is turned into immunoglobulin and albumin medicines sold by Grifols. Based in Phoenix, Arizona, it was part of Talecris and later Grifols after the 2011 acquisition. Local-community brand for donors, with no mass consumer profile.

Digital musculoskeletal clinic that treats joint and muscle pain, back pain and pelvic health through a mobile app with exercise therapy, wearable sensors and coaching by physical therapists, sold to employers, health plans and insurers. Based in San Francisco, founded in 2015, and listed on the NYSE (HNGE) since a 2025 IPO, having been valued at USD 6.2 billion privately. Millions of members. Consumer-facing in employer plans, moderate US brand awareness.

Canadian gold producer headquartered in Vancouver and listed on the TSX and Nasdaq Stockholm (LUG), operating the Fruta del Norte mine in south-eastern Ecuador, which produces about 450,000 ounces of gold per year, and exploring nearby projects. B2B commodity producer with a strong investor brand but low consumer awareness.

Chinese digital healthcare platform based in Beijing offering online consultations with doctors, health content, appointment booking and e-pharmacy services to patients across China. Connected operations platform, Samsara, based in San Francisco and listed on the NYSE (IOT), that sells Internet-of-Things sensors, dashcams, GPS trackers and cloud software to fleets, construction, utilities, food distribution and field services, helping them track vehicles, equipment and driver safety. Founded in 2015 by Sanjit Biswal and John Bicket, with annual recurring revenue above USD 1.5 billion. Customers are enterprises. B2B brand known in logistics, and it has sponsored sports properties.

Medical device company in Irvine, California, which developed implantable sacral neuromodulation systems for urinary and bowel incontinence, notably the r-SNM System with a rechargeable battery. B2B software brand known in the insurance technology sector, with no consumer profile.

US bank holding company based in Englewood, Colorado, parent of InBank, which provides commercial and personal banking, mortgage and agricultural lending to customers in Colorado, New Mexico, Wyoming and Kansas. Regional bank brand with limited awareness beyond its markets.

Bangladeshi lubricants company, MJL Bangladesh, based in Dhaka and listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange, which blends and sells Mobil-branded engine oils and industrial lubricants in Bangladesh under licence from ExxonMobil, and is controlled by the Jamuna Group. Australian health insurer, nib Holdings (nib health funds), based in Newcastle, New South Wales, and listed on the ASX (NHF), offering private health cover, travel insurance and international student and worker health cover in Australia and New Zealand. Well-known consumer brand in Australia with a history of sports sponsorship.

Indian small finance bank, Ujjivan Small Finance Bank, based in Bengaluru and listed on the NSE and BSE, offering microloans, savings accounts, deposits and housing and MSME loans, mainly to underbanked customers and small businesses in India. Recognised consumer finance brand in India, though regional and focused on rural and semi-urban markets.

Turkish power producer, Aksa Energy, based in Istanbul and listed on Borsa Istanbul, owned by Kazanci Holding. Israeli residential real estate developer, Azorim, based in Tel Aviv and listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, which builds apartment towers, housing projects and urban renewal schemes in Israel and has had projects abroad, including in Europe. Chilean bank, Banco Itau Chile, based in Las Condes, Santiago, formed when Itau Unibanco of Brazil took control of CorpBanca in 2016, offering retail, corporate, investment and wealth banking in Chile and Colombia. A major mid-sized Chilean bank, well known domestically though with a lower profile than the market leaders.

Indian housing finance company, Can Fin Homes, based in Bengaluru and listed on the NSE and BSE, promoted by Canara Bank, which provides home loans and loans against property to salaried and self-employed households, mostly in south India. Strong regional brand in housing finance, advertising largely through banks and local media.

Polish real estate investor and developer, Cavatina Holding, based in Krakow, which develops and owns office buildings, retail and logistics parks in Poland and Central Europe, selling or leasing space to businesses and investors. French energy company, La Francaise de l'Energie, based in Pontpierre in Lorraine and listed on Euronext Growth Paris, which produces gas from coal mine methane and works on capturing methane from old Lorraine coal seams, selling it as natural gas and electricity. Louisiana bank holding company, Home Bancorp, based in Lafayette and listed on Nasdaq (HBCP), parent of Home Bank, which provides consumer and commercial banking, mortgages and wealth management through dozens of branches in Louisiana, Texas and Mississippi. Swedish real estate company, K-Fast Holding, based in Hassleholm in southern Sweden, that owns and develops residential and commercial property, with a growing portfolio in the Skane region and beyond. Pennsylvania bank holding company, LINKBANCORP, based in Camp Hill and listed on Nasdaq (LNKB), parent of LINKBANK, which offers commercial and consumer banking, using a branch-light model, in central Pennsylvania, Philadelphia and nearby areas. New Jersey bank holding company, Northfield Bancorp, based in Woodbridge and listed on Nasdaq (NFBK), parent of Northfield Bank, which offers retail and commercial banking, multifamily and commercial real estate lending in New Jersey, Staten Island, Brooklyn and Pennsylvania through dozens of branches. Swedish satellite communications company, Ovzon, based in Solna near Stockholm, operating the Ovzon 3 geostationary satellite and providing broadband connectivity for military, government and security customers worldwide, including mobile terminals. B2B and defence-focused brand with no consumer profile and no obvious sponsorship interest.

Bangladeshi pharmaceutical company, Renata PLC, based in Dhaka and listed on the Dhaka and Chittagong stock exchanges, manufacturing branded generics, animal health products and vaccines, and exporting to dozens of countries. B2B and prescription brand with limited direct consumer awareness.

Thai real estate developer, SC Asset Corporation, based in Bangkok and listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SC), building detached houses, townhomes and condominiums for middle and upper income buyers, with sales of tens of billions of baht a year. US medical device company, Tivic Health Systems, listed on Nasdaq (TIVC), which sells ClearUP, a handheld bioelectronic device for sinus pain and congestion relief, sold directly to consumers online and through retailers. Zambian food producer, Zambeef Products, based in Lusaka and listed on the Lusaka Securities Exchange, operating beef, chicken, pork, dairy and milling businesses, with retail butcheries and the Zamleather and Zamchick brands. Virginia bank holding company, Chain Bridge Bancorp, based in McLean and listed on the NYSE (CBNA) since a 2024 IPO, parent of Chain Bridge Bank, which provides banking, treasury and trust services to individuals, businesses and political campaigns and committees in the Washington DC area. Customers also include political organisations. Founded in 2006. Small, specialised bank with low public profile outside Washington.

US digital media and creator platform company, Creatd, based in Fort Lee, New Jersey, whose Vocal platform lets writers and creators publish stories and earn money, along with owned media brands and a creator-focused e-commerce business. Listed on Nasdaq earlier and later shifted to over-the-counter markets after financial strain. Revenue is small and mostly from subscriptions and advertising. Limited public brand awareness.

Colorado-based wealth management and banking group, First Western Financial, listed on Nasdaq (MYFW), which provides integrated wealth planning, trust, investment and private banking services to high-net-worth individuals, families and businesses in Colorado, Arizona, Wyoming, Montana and California. Turkish wind power producer, Galata Wind Enerji, based in Istanbul and listed on Borsa Istanbul (GWIND), which owns and operates wind farms in Turkey, selling electricity under the country's renewable support schemes and market prices. Irish shipping and logistics group, Irish Continental Group, based in Dublin and listed on Euronext Dublin, operating Irish Ferries passenger and freight ferries between Ireland, the UK and France, and Eucon container shipping and terminal services in Dublin and Cork. Customers are holidaymakers, hauliers and freight forwarders. Irish Ferries is a well-known consumer brand in Ireland and the UK, and has a history of sports sponsorship.

Canadian building technology company, Kontrol Technologies, based in Vaughan, Ontario, selling smart building and indoor air quality systems, building automation controls, energy management and monitoring services, and emissions monitoring for industrial customers. It grew through acquisitions in Canada, the US and Middle East. Listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange. Customers are property owners and industrial firms. B2B brand with low public awareness.

Indian software company, Newgen Software Technologies, based in New Delhi and listed on the NSE and BSE, selling low-code process automation, content management and customer communication platforms to banks, insurers, governments and healthcare organisations. Founded in 1992. Customers are enterprises in India, Asia, Africa, Europe and the US. B2B software brand with good recognition among bank technology buyers but none among consumers.

Oil sands extraction technology company, Petroteq Energy, which developed a water-based process for extracting oil from oil sands in Utah's Uinta Basin, with an office in Sherman Oaks, California. Listed in Canada and the US, it was hit by accounting restatements and regulatory action in 2021 and its operations were scaled back. B2B energy technology company with a damaged investor reputation and no consumer profile.
